events.title: Carloman dies, leaving Charlemagne sole king of the Franks
events.description: Carloman I, Charlemagne's brother and co-ruler, died suddenly. Charlemagne took over his kingdom, and Carloman's widow fled with her sons to the Lombards.
events.html: Carloman I, Charlemagne's brother and co-ruler, died suddenly. Charlemagne took over his kingdom, and Carloman's widow fled with her sons to the Lombards.

events.title: The Observer is first published
events.description: The first issue of The Observer appeared in London. It is the world's oldest Sunday newspaper still in publication.
events.html: The first issue of The Observer appeared in London. It is the world's oldest Sunday newspaper still in publication.

events.title: The National Grange is founded
events.description: Oliver Kelley and colleagues founded the Order of Patrons of Husbandry, known as the Grange, in Washington. It became a powerful voice for farmers against railway rates and monopolies.
events.html: Oliver Kelley and colleagues founded the Order of Patrons of Husbandry, known as the Grange, in Washington. It became a powerful voice for farmers against railway rates and monopolies.

events.title: The Mary Celeste is found drifting and abandoned
events.description: The crew of the Dei Gratia found the American brigantine Mary Celeste sailing unmanned in the Atlantic, her cargo intact and lifeboat gone. The fate of the ten people aboard has never been explained.
events.html: The crew of the Dei Gratia found the American brigantine Mary Celeste sailing unmanned in the Atlantic, her cargo intact and lifeboat gone. The fate of the ten people aboard has never been explained.

events.title: Pan Am ceases operations
events.description: Pan American World Airways flew its last flight after 64 years. The airline had pioneered transoceanic air travel and launched the Boeing 747, but it never recovered from deregulation, recession and the Lockerbie bombing.
